text: Hi Jordan, thanks for joining. How's your day going so far?
So, to get started, can you tell me a little bit about yourself?
What made you interested in this role here at Kestrel Pay?
Great, thanks. So just for context, our team is about twelve engineers split across two squads, and we mostly work in Go and TypeScript.
Tell me about a time you had to deal with a major production incident.
candidateSaid: Sure. The big one was Black Friday 2022 at Quayside. Consumer lag on our shipment events grew to about two hours, so customers weren't seeing tracking updates. I led the response, we rolled back a deploy and scaled up consumers, and we were caught up in about six hours.

text: And what was the actual root cause? What did you change afterward so it wouldn't happen again?
Why did you pick Kafka over something like RabbitMQ for that pipeline?
Have you worked with Kubernetes in production?
How would you design a rate limiter for a public API that handles around fifty thousand requests per second?
Tell me about a disagreement you had with a teammate and how you handled it.
Can you walk me through how you'd debug a memory leak in a Node.js service, and how you'd keep it from happening again?
candidateSaid: I'd start by confirming it's a leak with memory graphs, then take heap snapshots a few minutes apart and compare them. At Tallgrass that's how I found an unbounded in-memory cache in the scheduling API.

text: Why not just give the service more memory and restart it on a schedule?
What would you say is your biggest weakness?
What are your salary expectations for this role?
Where do you see yourself in five years?
Okay. Mm-hm. Let me just, uh, pull up my notes here.
We've got a few minutes left. Do you have any questions for us?
